zh.q: 盒里的碳球为什么要留 4 个接口，氢球只有 1 个？
zh.concl: 碳原子最外层有 4 个电子，能形成 4 个共价键；氢只能形成 1 个。这就是「碳四价」——所以链状烷烃的分子式是 CₙH₂ₙ₊₂。
points: 碳原子以最外层的 4 个电子，分别与别的原子形成 4 个共价键。
碳与碳之间也能成键，可以成单键、双键或三键。
氢原子只能形成 1 个共价键，所以氢球只有 1 个接口。

zh.q: 甲烷的 4 个氢，凭什么说它们完全一样？
zh.concl: 甲烷是正四面体：碳在中心，4 个氢在 4 个顶点，键角 109°28′（也就是 109.47°），5 个原子不在同一平面。正因为 4 个顶点完全等价，4 个氢才完全一样。（键角数值见选择性必修 2「物质结构与性质」；必修第二册只要求「4 个键相互之间的夹角相等」。）
points: 甲烷不是平面正方形，是正四面体。
4 个 C—H 键长都是 109 pm，6 对 H—C—H 角都是 109°28′。
5 个原子不在同一平面上。

zh.q: 把甲烷的两个氢换成氯，能有几种搭法？
zh.concl: 二氯甲烷只有一种结构，没有同分异构体——模型按正四面体搭，4 个顶点完全等价，换成哪两个氢都是同一种结构。教材的实验活动8【问题和讨论】2 就是用球棍模型验证这件事。
points: 正四面体 4 个顶点等价，换哪两个氢都得到同一个分子。
模型按正四面体搭，4 个顶点等价；换哪两个 H 都是同一种结构。（拓展：真实的 CH₂Cl₂ 不是正四面体，Cl—C—Cl 约 112°，所以本课不给它报键角。）
如果甲烷真是平面正方形，二氯甲烷就会有邻位、对位两种结构。

zh.q: 把乙烷的 C—C 键扭一下，分子还是同一个吗？
zh.concl: C—C 单键可以绕键轴自由旋转；转的只是同一个分子的不同姿态，分子本身没变，不算同分异构。双键、三键就转不动——这就是乙烯被压成一个平面、乙炔被压成一条线的原因。
points: 单键可以绕键轴旋转，转的过程中化学键不会被破坏。
旋转改变的只是构象，分子还是同一个分子。
（拓展 · 选必3 p.6）单键是 σ 键，σ 键可绕键轴旋转；双键、三键里有 π 键，π 键不能绕键轴旋转。

zh.q: 碳原子能不能一个接一个接下去？
zh.concl: 碳原子可以相互连成链，链越长原子越多；链状饱和烃的通式是 CₙH₂ₙ₊₂。链变长了，可每个碳还是四面体、键角还是 109°28′。
points: 碳可以连成直链，也可以连成带支链或成环的骨架。
原子数随碳原子数增加，键角始终不变。
链状烷烃通式 CₙH₂ₙ₊₂，相邻同系物相差一个 CH₂。

zh.q: 同样 4 个碳、10 个氢，为什么能搭出两个不同的分子？
zh.concl: 分子式相同、结构不同的两种化合物互为同分异构体：正丁烷是直链，异丁烷带支链。骨架不同，性质也就不同——正丁烷沸点 −0.5 ℃，异丁烷沸点 −11.6 ℃。
points: 同分异构体：分子式相同、结构不同。
正丁烷是直链，异丁烷带支链，末端甲基 2 个对 3 个。

zh.q: 为什么乙烯的 6 个原子挤在一个平面上，乙炔的 4 个原子排成一条线？
zh.concl: 乙烯里两个碳之间是双键，转不动，6 个原子被锁在同一个平面上，键角约 120°；乙炔里是三键，更转不动，4 个原子被锁成一条直线，键角 180°。拖「C—C 单键旋转角」它们纹丝不动——只剩乙烷那样的单键才转得动。
points: 乙烯 6 个原子共平面，键角约 120°。
乙炔 4 个原子共线，键角 180°。
C=C 133 pm、C≡C 120 pm，三键比双键更短。
（拓展 · 选必3 p.34、p.37）双键是 1 个 σ 键 + 1 个 π 键，三键是 1 个 σ 键 + 2 个 π 键；碳原子分别是 sp²、sp 杂化。

zh.q: 苯的 6 个碳碳键，为什么说它们完全一样长？
zh.concl: 苯是平面正六边形，12 个原子共平面，键间夹角都是 120°。6 个碳碳键完全等同，键长都是 139 pm，正好夹在单键 154 pm 和双键 133 pm 中间——所以苯里没有单双键交替。
points: 苯 12 个原子共平面，正六边形，键间夹角都是 120°。
6 个碳碳键等长，都是 139 pm。
139 pm 介于单键 154 pm 和双键 133 pm 之间。

zh.q: 换你搭：把 C₄H₁₀ 的另一种结构调出来
zh.concl: 4 个碳的烷烃有两种结构：正丁烷是直链，异丁烷带支链。它们分子式都是 C₄H₁₀，可骨架不同，是两种不同的化合物。
points: 分子式相同、结构不同，就是同分异构体。
4 个碳的烷烃有两种结构。
碳骨架不同，物理性质就不同。
考核没过就回第 6 步，重看两种骨架的差别。

en.q: Why does the carbon ball in the box have 4 sockets, but the hydrogen ball only 1?
en.concl: A carbon atom has 4 outer electrons and can form 4 covalent bonds; hydrogen can form only 1. This is "tetravalent carbon", which is why open-chain alkanes have the formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
points: A carbon atom uses its 4 outer electrons to form 4 covalent bonds with other atoms.
Carbon can also bond to carbon, through single, double or triple bonds.
A hydrogen atom can form only 1 covalent bond, so the hydrogen ball has just 1 socket.

en.q: How can we say the 4 hydrogens of methane are exactly alike?
en.concl: Methane is a regular tetrahedron: carbon at the center, 4 hydrogens at the 4 vertices, bond angle 109°28′ (that is, 109.47°), and the 5 atoms are not in one plane. Because the 4 vertices are fully equivalent, the 4 hydrogens are exactly alike. (The bond-angle value comes from Elective 2 "Structure and Properties of Matter"; Compulsory Book 2 only requires that "the 4 bonds make equal angles with each other".)
points: Methane is not a flat square; it is a regular tetrahedron.
All 4 C—H bonds are 109 pm long, and all 6 H—C—H angles are 109°28′.
The 5 atoms are not in the same plane.

en.q: Replace two hydrogens of methane with chlorine. How many ways can it be built?
en.concl: Dichloromethane has only one structure and no isomers. Built as a regular tetrahedron, the model has 4 fully equivalent vertices, so replacing any two hydrogens gives the same structure. Question 2 of the textbook's Lab Activity 8 "Questions and discussion" uses ball-and-stick models to check exactly this.
points: The 4 vertices of a tetrahedron are equivalent, so replacing any two hydrogens gives the same molecule.

The model is built as a regular tetrahedron with 4 equivalent vertices, so replacing any two H gives the same structure. (Extension: real CH₂Cl₂ is not a regular tetrahedron; Cl—C—Cl is about 112°, so this lesson does not give it a bond angle.)
If methane really were a flat square, dichloromethane would have two structures: adjacent and opposite.

en.q: Twist the C—C bond of ethane. Is it still the same molecule?
en.concl: A C—C single bond can rotate freely about its axis; rotation only gives different poses of the same molecule, so it is not isomerism. Double and triple bonds cannot rotate, which is why ethene is locked into a plane and ethyne into a line.
points: A single bond can rotate about its axis without breaking the bond.
Rotation changes only the conformation; it is still the same molecule.
(Extension · Elective 3 p.6) A single bond is a σ bond, which can rotate about its axis; double and triple bonds contain π bonds, which cannot.

en.q: Can carbon atoms keep linking one after another?
en.concl: Carbon atoms can link into chains; the longer the chain, the more atoms. Open-chain saturated hydrocarbons follow CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. The chain grows, yet every carbon is still tetrahedral with bond angles of 109°28′.
points: Carbon can form straight chains, branched chains or rings.
The atom count rises with the number of carbons; the bond angle never changes.
Open-chain alkanes follow CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, and neighboring homologues differ by one CH₂.

en.q: With the same 4 carbons and 10 hydrogens, why can two different molecules be built?
en.concl: Two compounds with the same formula but different structures are isomers: n-butane is a straight chain, isobutane is branched. Different skeletons mean different properties: n-butane boils at −0.5 ℃, isobutane at −11.6 ℃.
points: Isomers: same molecular formula, different structure.
n-Butane is a straight chain, isobutane is branched: 2 versus 3 end methyl groups.
Their boiling points differ: −0.5 ℃ versus −11.6 ℃.

en.q: Why are the 6 atoms of ethene squeezed into one plane, and the 4 atoms of ethyne in a line?
en.concl: In ethene the two carbons share a double bond that cannot rotate, so the 6 atoms are locked in one plane with bond angles of about 120°. In ethyne it is a triple bond, even more rigid, locking the 4 atoms in a straight line at 180°. Drag "C—C single-bond rotation" and they do not budge; only single bonds like ethane's can rotate.
points: The 6 atoms of ethene are coplanar, bond angle about 120°.
The 4 atoms of ethyne are collinear, bond angle 180°.
C=C 133 pm, C≡C 120 pm: a triple bond is shorter than a double bond.
(Extension · Elective 3 p.34, p.37) A double bond is 1 σ bond + 1 π bond, a triple bond is 1 σ bond + 2 π bonds; the carbons are sp² and sp hybridized respectively.

en.q: Why are the 6 carbon-carbon bonds of benzene said to be exactly the same length?
en.concl: Benzene is a planar regular hexagon: 12 atoms are coplanar, and every angle between bonds is 120°. All 6 carbon-carbon bonds are identical at 139 pm, right between a single bond (154 pm) and a double bond (133 pm), so benzene has no alternating single and double bonds.
points: The 12 atoms of benzene are coplanar in a regular hexagon, with all bond angles 120°.
All 6 carbon-carbon bonds are equal, 139 pm each.
139 pm lies between a single bond (154 pm) and a double bond (133 pm).

en.q: Your turn: bring up the other structure of C₄H₁₀
en.concl: The 4-carbon alkane has two structures: n-butane is a straight chain, isobutane is branched. Both are C₄H₁₀, but their skeletons differ, so they are two different compounds.
points: Same formula, different structure: that makes isomers.
The 4-carbon alkane has two structures.
A different carbon skeleton gives different physical properties.
If you fail the check, go back to step 6 and review the difference between the two skeletons.
